aspect: Iran will not take involuntary returnees
description: Foreign minister Mohammad Javad Zarif publicly rejected a proposed repatriation deal with Australia in 2016, saying Iran cannot force anybody to return but accepts citizens who come back voluntarily. The deal would have covered almost 9,000 people.
energy_note: Neither country will take you, and one of them has you.

description: ASF17 arrived in 2013 and was detained continuously from 2014. He refused to consent to return to Iran or to meet Iranian authorities to obtain a travel document, but was willing to be removed to any other country in the world.

During the litigation he disclosed for the first time that he is bisexual, and that his refusal rested on fear of returning to Iran, where sex between men is illegal and can attract the death penalty.
energy_note: Forced to disclose the thing you fled, in open court, to explain why you will not go back.

aspect: EXAMPLE - 'the capacity to change his mind'
description: The High Court distinguished the earlier NZYQ ruling and held his detention lawful, because detention remained for the purpose of facilitating departure. The justices noted he had 'the capacity to change his mind' but chose not to. Unanimous.
energy_note: Your own refusal to be persecuted, reclassified as your choice to stay in prison.

description: Commentators estimated up to 200 people could remain indefinitely detained as a result, and legislation before parliament would have let the minister apply a blanket ban on nationals of countries that refuse deportees - such as Iran.

In January 2026 the UN Committee against Torture found Australia failed to protect an Iranian asylum seeker from torture and ill-treatment across years of detention, first on Manus Island and later on the mainland. He arrived by boat in 2013 and says he was held about three years in harsh conditions and subjected to serious violence.

aspect: EXAMPLE - eight years on six-month visas
description: A separate group recognised as refugees, unable to return to Iran and with nowhere else to go, were evacuated to Australia for urgent medical care between 2015 and 2018 and remain on short-term bridging visas, reapplying every six months.
energy_note: A life renewed in six-month increments.
